title: Taiwan's digital affairs ministry says government network repels an average of 2.8 million cyberattacks daily
date_note: Taiwan News (24 November) says the ministry gave the figures on Monday; the page gives no earlier day.
summary: Taiwan News reports that Taiwan's Ministry of Digital Affairs released figures saying the government network repels an average of 2.8 million cyberattacks daily. The article says most of the attacks come from China, Russia, North Korea and Iran. The figures followed minister Lin Yi-jing's interview with Der Standard in Vienna.
plain: Taiwan's digital affairs ministry says its government network fends off an average of 2.8 million cyberattacks every day, according to Taiwan News.
exec: The ministry's figure, as reported by Taiwan News, shows the scale of attack traffic against Taiwan's government network.

evidence.quote: Taiwan's government network repels an average of 2.8 million cyberattacks daily.

validation.note: Taiwan News and Focus Taiwan (CNA) each report the Ministry of Digital Affairs figure (Focus Taiwan: about 2.8 million per day, from minister Lin Yi-ching's Der Standard interview, content released by the ministry on 23 November). The ministry's own release was not read.

review.note: Compared title, 2.8 million figure, countries, Monday 23 Nov date, Der Standard context against Taiwan News and Focus Taiwan
